newsitem.title: EGYPT: Shares rise in thin trade on Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Shares rise in thin trade on Cairo bourse.

text.p: Egyptian share prices reversed their recent trend, rising on Monday in thin trade on the Cairo bourse, the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) report showed.
"The market is a little bit thin due to a lack of foreign institutional buying," said Tarek Lotfy of Intercapital.
"They want to see stability in prices before they start buying... They still love prospects in Egypt," he added.
The CMA overall index closed 2.34 points up at 363.51 points in trade worth 37.63 million pounds ($11.08 million).

Prices have been on the slide in general for the past three months, but Lotfy said this was normal. "The market needs correction. It's very healthy," Lotfy told Reuters. "Prices are more realistic and more attractive now."
Cements regained their position on the list of most active shares, despite ending either down or unchanged.

Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA closed 2.3 pounds down at 72.1, when shares worth 3.41 million pounds changed hands. Amriyah Cement, the second most active, closed at 83.05 pounds, down 0.57 in 3.28 million pounds worth of trade.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement ended unchanged at 90.5 pounds, after shares worth 2.27 million were traded.
Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN was active ending 1.49 pounds up at 119.99. Shares worth 1.98 million changed hands.
Egyptian American Bank (EAB) regained some of its recent losses, rising 1.84 pounds at 131. The bank has good performing loans and solid management, said Lotfy of EAB's potential.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 515.84 from 515.06 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms also rose to 263.98 from 261.59 points.
Out of 87 shares traded, 33 rose and 33 fell while 21 ended unchanged.
